title: Bias, Confounding and Effect Modification: Exam Table
subject: PSM
preview: Selection bias arises from how participants are sampled or retained; information bias arises from measurement errors.
quickRevision: Selection bias arises from how participants are sampled or retained; information bias arises from measurement errors.
Effect modification occurs when the effect genuinely differs across levels of another variable.
Randomization, design restrictions, stratification and multivariable adjustment address different threats to inference.

sections.title: Recognize the core pattern
points: Selection bias arises from how participants are sampled or retained; information bias arises from measurement errors.
Confounding occurs when another variable distorts an exposure-outcome association.

sections.title: Clinical examination and interpretation
points: Effect modification occurs when the effect genuinely differs across levels of another variable.
Randomization, design restrictions, stratification and multivariable adjustment address different threats to inference.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Effect modification should be described rather than simply adjusted away as if always an error.

quiz.question: What is effect modification?
options: A real difference in effect across groups
quiz.explanation: A real difference in effect across groups. Effect modification occurs when the effect genuinely differs across levels of another variable.
